mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate foreign investor or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate registrar in the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the country of origin is a Hague Apostille Convention member, obtain a certificate of incorporation from the registrar and attach an apostille issued by the designated competent authority; do not add Chinese consular legalization. If the country of origin is not a member, have the registrar copy certified and legalized by the country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then by the PRC Embassy or Consulate in that country. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Incumbency) of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or commercial registry authority of the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Use Hague Apostille route for apostille-convention states, with the apostille attached to the registry certificate. Use consular legalization route only for non-member states, starting with notarial or registrar certification, then foreign MFA legalization, then PRC consular legalization. Never chain the apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the WFOE incorporation and appointing a power-of-attorney agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent entity and a notary public in the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized board resolution is submitted either to the designated competent authority for an apostille (for Apostille Convention states) or, if the origin state is not a member, to that state's foreign ministry and then the PRC Embassy/Consulate for legalization. The two authentication protocols must not be combined or duplicated.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional document) of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company, certified by a notary or registrar in the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A certified copy of the articles must carry a notarial certificate. For Apostille states, the notary certificate must be apostilled. For non-member states, it must be legalized by the foreign ministry and then the PRC consulate. These methods are alternative and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the foreign parent's bank for KYC/UBO verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank of the foreign parent entity, under officer signature and bank seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter is issued on bank letterhead and, if required by Chinese banks or SAMR, authenticated through one parallel route only: apostille for member states, or notarization plus foreign MFA verification plus PRC embassy/consulate legalization for non-member states. The letter must be dated no earlier than 90 days before filing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before engagement, every UBO, director, shareholder, signatory and senior manager must be screened at initial instruction, before name clearance, and immediately before filing against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and China's domestic AML/CFT sanctions and high-risk jurisdiction lists. PEP status must be checked for heads of state, government ministers, senior judges, military leaders, senior state-owned-enterprise executives, their family members and close associates. Any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence, independent source-of-funds proof, documented senior-management sign-off and, if unresolved, refusal to onboard. Continuous monitoring for sanctions-list updates, adverse media and transaction red flags remains mandatory from the first intake through the entire pre-incorporation period and for 180 days after incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation National Enterprise Name Online Declaration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE legal name must be declared in simplified Chinese characters and no English may be used in the registered name. The mandatory four-tier formula is [Administrative Division] + [Distinctive Trade Name] + [Industry/Activity Description] + [Company Type], for example Shanghai AB Sodium-Ion Battery Co., Ltd. A foreign investor may use a phonetic transliteration (pinyin or commonly used transliteration) of its own corporate name as the distinctive token. Homonyms, identical or similar names in the same industry, and misleading or damaging content are prohibited. If an English name is desired, it may be used only commercially and in bank/tax filings after registration, not as part of the SAMR-approved legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An approved name reservation may be extended only by filing a fresh declaration before the 30-day window expires and within the same SAMR system; there is no automatic extension. If the SAMR name declaration is rejected, the applicant must first correct any duplicate or sensitive token issue in a new declaration, preserving the filing reference number. For an administrative appeal, the applicant or law firm files a written administrative reconsideration request with the next-higher Administration for Market Regulation or the local People's Government within 10 working days after rejection, attaching evidence of the distinctive trade name, industry classification, foreign-investor name linkage, and any ministerial approval obtained for a sensitive token. The reconsideration authority must issue a decision within 60 days. If it rejects the request, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months, or resubmit a new name declaration using a different distinctive token at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered address for a WFOE engaged in sodium-ion battery cell manufacturing. SAMR requires a valid property ownership certificate or a lease contract with a definite physical location; the tax bureau requires a real business site for VAT invoice control and file inspection; and banks require physical-visit confirmation before opening corporate accounts. A virtual office can be used only as an additional correspondence or administrative satellite address after the actual registered address satisfies the factory-floor and facility requirements of the production license, and the landlord must issue a written consent for business registration use.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (1) company nameplate at the registered address; (2) lease agreement with the same legal entity as named in the business license; (3) production equipment and safety permits consistent with ISIC 2720; (4) accounting and payroll records at the premises; (5) social insurance registration for local employees; and (6) environmental protection, fire safety and battery-waste disposal records. Quantified risk: 85 to 95 percent for a virtual-office or residential address in a manufacturing WFOE during the first 12 months; 45 to 60 percent for a genuine leased factory in the first year; 25 percent or lower after an established industrial-zone operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (Revised 2023, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 23-33, 37, 41, 46, 49, 50 and 51; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2019), Articles 4, 9, 12 and 28; Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration (2021); Negative List for Foreign Investment Access (2024 edition)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Municipal Market Regulation Administration with jurisdiction over the registered office; operation through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company (Company Registration Application Form) together with the Foreign Investment Information Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for an ordinary WFOE under PRC law. The revised Company Law adopts subscribed capital with no statutory minimum. The WFOE must, however, state a registered capital that is reasonably matched to the total investment under the local Foreign Investment guidance and must specify a contribution period not exceeding the legal ceiling (commonly up to 30 years) in the Articles of Association. No statutory backend escrow account is mandated; the sole shareholder may make in-kind or cash contributions and, where requested by banks or counterparties, obtain a capital verification report from a licensed PRC certified public accountant.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING OF SODIUM CELL (CHINA) NEW ENERGY CO., LTD. (the 'Company'), adopted by unanimous written consent of all directors at [●] [●], China, on [●], 20[●].

WHEREAS the Company is a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise desiring to organize its management and complete the post-registration formalities required by the Company Law of the People's Republic of China.

IT IS RESOLVED:

1. Registered Capital and Share Subscription. The Board confirms that the registered capital of the Company is [●] RMB, subscribed in full by the sole shareholder. The Board authorizes the legal representative and Chief Financial Officer to open a designated capital verification account in the name of the Company, to receive the subscription proceeds, and to issue share subscription certificates. The Board further authorizes the engagement of a licensed PRC certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report if required by the bank or the shareholders.

2. Adoption of Constitutional Documents. The Board approves the final text of the Articles of Association and all ancillary constitutional documents to be filed with the Market Regulation Administration. The legal representative is directed to execute the filing instruments, make all statutory declarations, and obtain the business license endorsement reflecting the adopted constitutional documents.

3. Registered Office. The Board adopts [●], [●], China as the registered office of the Company. The Board approves the execution of the lease agreement, the property ownership certificate verification, and the registration of the official address in all corporate records and registers.

4. Banking Authorization. The Board designates [●] Bank, [●] branch, as the principal basic deposit bank and foreign exchange settlement bank. The Board authorizes the Chairman, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting in any two-signature combination, to open bank accounts, sign payment instructions, negotiate loans or letters of credit, access online banking, and execute related financial instruments.

5. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appoints [●] as Chairman and Legal Representative, [●] as General Manager/Chief Executive Officer, [●] as Chief Financial Officer, and [●] as Company Secretary. Each appointment is effective immediately and shall continue until the first general meeting of shareholders. The officers are authorized, jointly within the limits of the Articles, to hire employees, sign customer and supplier contracts, apply for industrial permits, and deal with state agencies.

6. General Implementation Authority. The Board authorizes all officers to complete the EIA permitting, fire safety approvals, pollution discharge permits, tax registration, social insurance registration, and any other licences required for the manufacture of sodium-ion battery cells. This resolution may be handed to third parties as conclusive evidence of the authority conferred. The first general meeting of shareholders shall ratify these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval, Foreign-Investment Screening and Business Scope Alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Administration for Market Regulation through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit, through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), a name pre-approval application and a proposed business scope expressly limited to sodium-ion battery cell manufacturing under ISIC 2720/GB 4754 industry code 3841. The scope must avoid activities contained in the 2024 Negative List for Foreign Investment Access. Simultaneously file the Foreign Investment Information Report so that the pre-establishment national treatment record is created. If the parent entity is a foreign corporation, deliver a notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolution authorizing establishment, and power of attorney appointing a Chinese agent or law firm. The proposed Chinese company name must contain a distinctive trade name and the form 'Limited Liability Company'.
required_dossiers: Name Pre-Approval Application (Form SM-01)
Proposed Articles of Association (draft in Chinese)
Business Scope Description referencing GB/T 4754-2017 and ISIC 2720
Notarized and legalized Certificate of Incorporation of the sole corporate shareholder
Certificate of Good Standing (issued within 90 days)
Parent board resolution authorizing the WFOE establishment
Power of Attorney to the Chinese filing agent
Chinese translation of all foreign-language documents
Landlord lease intent letter and property ownership certificate copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the platform queries the name or scope, withdraw and re-file with corrected language within 2 business days. If a forbidden negative-list item is detected, restructure the business scope or propose a joint venture; if the name conflicts, choose up to 3 alternative names in priority order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing with SAMR and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Enterprise Registration Window or online Chinese Government Service Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name pre-approval, execute the final Articles of Association and all corporate formation documents, including the resolution of the sole shareholder approving the registered capital and first directors. Submit the establishment registration application to the SAMR local office, together with the name certificate, lease, identity documents, and the Foreign Investment Information Report. The registry will cross-screen with the public security and national security authorities; if no issue is found, the registry issues a unified Business License with a Unified Social Credit Code. The date of issuance is the legal date of incorporation of the WFOE. The foreign parent's notarization documents must remain valid for at least 6 months, and if expired, a new notarization must be supplied before submission.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Establishment Registration
Approved Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
Name Pre-Approval Certificate
Proof of registered address (lease contract, ownership certificate, and landlord consent)
Identification certificates of the legal representative, directors, supervisors, and general manager
Appointment letters and resignation letters of directors/supervisors/managers
Original foreign-investor notarized/legalized documents with Chinese translation
Foreign Investment Information Report as integrated in the filing system
Receipt of name approval and any verification codes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an exigent review or query is issued, respond and cure within the construction period indicated by the SAMR (usually 15 days). For missing or conflicting notarizations, re-submit through the specific window; if business license issuance is suspended, amend the Articles of Association or governance lists and restart the step without additional name reservation if the name remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seal Carving, Bank Account Opening, Tax and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) - authorized seal engraving units; licensed Chinese banks and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); the State Taxation Administration local office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receipt of the Business License, the legal representative must obtain the unified social credit code and arrange for carving of the official company seal, finance seal, invoice seal, contract seal, and the legal representative's personal seal. These seals are rendered at a PSB-designated engraving service and their impressions are recorded with the local public security bureau. The company should then open a basic deposit account at a licensed bank, with a separate foreign exchange account for trade settlement if cells are exported. Under the bank's account opening process, the anti-money laundering risk assessment will be performed, and the target payment rails Swift Wire and Letter of Credit can be set up. Complete tax registration with the local State Taxation Administration within 30 calendar days, identify the VAT taxpayer type, invoice quota, and general taxpayer status; and register employees and housing fund accounts.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code
Articles of Association and shareholder resolution
Official company seal and finance seal (after carving)
Legal representative and authorized handler identity documents
Bank account opening application and AML/KYC forms
Tax registration form and business scope schedule
Foreign exchange settlement account application and import/export registration if applicable
Employee list and social insurance/housing fund registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due diligence for medium-risk manufacturing, provide board resolutions, ultimate beneficial owner declarations, and source of funds structure. If the tax registration is not accepted, correct the registration forms and refile; late filings may attract minor penalties but can be remedied by submission of a reasonable explanation and payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Fire, Occupational Health and Industrial Licensing Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau; Fire and Rescue Department; Municipal Emergency Management Bureau; provincial market regulation department for industrial product licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing factory fit-out or production, the WFOE must classify the project under the Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment of Construction Projects (2021). For sodium-ion cell manufacturing, a full Environmental Impact Report is required when the project involves high-energy electrode processes, hazardous-chemical use, or significant discharge; otherwise an Environmental Impact Form is submitted and approved. After EIA approval, apply for the Pollution Discharge Permit covering wastewater, VOCs, and hazardous waste. Concurrently, submit fire safety design documents for review, install fire detection and suppression systems, and obtain the Fire Control Acceptance Inspection Certificate after completion. File occupational-disease hazard assessment and complete work safety pre-evaluation; install waste electrolyte containment, fire extinguishing supplies, and emergency ventilation. If the battery product falls within the current industrial product production license catalogue, apply to the provincial market regulation bureau; if not, proceed with conformity certification under applicable national standards.
required_dossiers: Construction project EIA classification form and EIA report or form
Public participation notices and comments (if required)
Pollution Discharge Permit application and pollutant discharge calculation tables
Fire protection design drawings and design institute stamp
Fire protection completion acceptance inspection application
Hazardous waste management plan and storage site layout
Occupational disease hazard project filing form
Work safety pre-evaluation report and emergency response plan
Sodium-ion battery cell production process flow and material safety data sheets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EIA is rejected or suspended, revise the impact assessment and resubmit with supplemented baseline data; if the pollution discharge permit is questioned, add monitoring plans and emission reduction commitments. For fire acceptance failure, remedy nonconformities with a certified fire protection engineer and re-inspect; if occupational hazard filing is incomplete, submit corrections and schedule medical surveillance for workers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and Municipal Bureau of Industry and Information Technology; designated approval windows for environmental and fire permits under the Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the Fire and Rescue Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Pollution Discharge Permit and Construction Project Environmental Impact Assessment Approval plus Fire Control Acceptance Inspection Certificate; optionally an Industrial Product Production License if the battery cell product is listed in the current PRC production license catalogue; otherwise a product conformity certificate under mandatory national standards

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 77 'Battery Manufacturing' under the Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment of Construction Projects (2021): large projects with metal electrode coatings, electrolytic solutions, or hazardous substance emissions are subject to a Full Environmental Impact Report (EIA Report) with public participation; general sodium-ion cell assembly/formation operations are subject to an Environmental Impact Form; ancillary storage-only operations may qualify as Registration Form.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with GB 30484-2013 (Emission Standard of Pollutants for the Battery Industry), GB 8978-1996 (Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard), GB 16297-1996 (Integrated Emission Standard of Air Pollutants), GB 37822-2019 (Volatile Organic Compounds Emission Standard for Industrial Enterprises) and GB 18597 (Hazardous Waste Storage Pollution Control Standard). Quantitative obligations typically include process wastewater pH 6-9, COD not exceeding 100 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 70 mg/L, ammonia nitrogen not exceeding 15 mg/L, total nickel and lead within the discharge permit limits, VOC abatement efficiency of at least 90%, and no unmanaged hazardous waste storage beyond one year. All numerical limits are determined in the site-specific discharge permit, but the plant must meet the strictest standard applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The factory must obtain a Fire Control Design Review and a Fire Control Completion Acceptance Inspection Certificate from the Fire and Rescue Department of the Ministry of Emergency Management before operation. The fire safety plan must address sodium-ion cell fire hazards, including Class D extinguishing agents, dry powder systems, battery thermal runaway containment, emergency egress and smoke management. Structural load inspections of battery racks and storage areas must be certified by a licensed structural engineer. In addition, the WFOE must complete an occupational-disease hazard project filing, a workplace safety pre-evaluation, and receive a work safety inspection under the Law on Work Safety and the Law on Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the nationwide Electronic Tax Bureau online portal (STA e-Tax platform) and the China International Trade Single Window for customs-related tax filings
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon business registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is automatically assigned a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which serves as the taxpayer identification number (TIN) for all tax purposes. Within 30 days after obtaining the business license, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the competent STA tax authority through the STA e-Tax portal, submitting the articles of association, SAMR business license, legal representative identity documents, registered address proof, bank account information, business scope details, foreign investor qualification/certificates, and appointment documents for the legal representative and financial officer. The STA will finalize the taxpayer registration record, determine the VAT taxpayer type (general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer), and activate the entity for VAT invoice issuance. The USCC is thereafter used as the VAT registration number and corporate income tax identifier for all filings, assessments, and refund procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Chinese resident enterprise; the WFOE limited liability company is taxed at entity level on worldwide income; no pass-through treatment to foreign shareholders)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or elective hybrid mismatch classification. The WFOE is mandatorily classified as a Chinese resident enterprise for corporate income tax purposes. Controlled foreign corporation rules and general anti-avoidance rules under the Enterprise Income Tax Law may recharacterize income or impose additional adjustments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) with export zero-rating implemented through VAT exemption and export tax rebate for eligible exported goods
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration is mandatory immediately upon business registration regardless of turnover. For compulsory general VAT taxpayer status, the statutory turnover threshold is annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000; below this threshold the WFOE may be registered as a small-scale taxpayer using the simplified 3% levy method or may voluntarily elect general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue VAT special invoices or VAT ordinary invoices through the STA-controlled electronic invoice system. Fully digitalised electronic invoices are cleared in near real time through the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform, with centrally allocated invoice numbers and direct digital transmission of invoice data to the tax authority under the Golden Tax System Phase IV. API-based direct e-invoicing is available for integrated enterprise resource planning systems. Paper VAT invoices, where still used, require tax authority invoice number allocation and the use of an approved fiscal control device. Anti-fraud controls include automatic invoice verification, exception screening, risk-based red flags, and mandatory blacklist reporting for abnormal invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of finished sodium-ion battery cells is eligible for VAT zero-rating, applied as exemption from output VAT plus refund of input VAT (export tax rebate), provided the goods are physically exported, customs-declared, sold to an overseas buyer, and the export proceeds are repatriated into China within the statutory foreign exchange deadline. The WFOE must be a VAT general taxpayer with export business filing and must submit a correct and truthful export declaration through the China International Trade Single Window. Zero-rating may also apply to qualifying offshore services or digital services where the services are rendered entirely outside China and the supporting contract, payment evidence, and service delivery documentation demonstrate overseas consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Customs Declaration / Bill of Entry) generated through the China International Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exportation of the battery cells from China
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Receipt Confirmation issued by a designated Chinese bank
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Export sales contract or purchase order between the WFOE and the overseas buyer
VAT invoice issued in accordance with export VAT regulations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and VAT refund claims are subject to post-clearance risk assessment, documentary verification, and tax audit. If the required customs, transport, invoice, or foreign exchange repatriation documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent, the export zero-rating is denied and the transaction is recharacterized as a domestic taxable sale, triggering VAT at 13%, recovery of any refunded input VAT, statutory late-payment surcharges, and administrative fines ranging from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under the Law of the People's Republic of China on Tax Administration and Collection. Fraudulent export VAT refund claims may constitute criminal fraud in obtaining export tax rebates under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, carrying fines, confiscation, and imprisonment; retrospective clawback may extend to all related input VAT credits, export rebate years, and affiliated party documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible for ordinary current-account trade and services, but convertibility is conditional on documentary verification through SAFE's electronic monitoring platform. Capital-account transactions, including FDI equity injections, shareholder loans, and cross-border guarantees, require registration, approval, or post-event reporting. The WFOE must complete an FDI registration certificate before opening a dedicated capital settlement account and is subject to the negative-list 'willing settlement' regime for converting foreign currency capital into RMB. Profit remittance to the overseas shareholder is allowed only after local statutory audit, corporate income tax settlement, dividend withholding tax settlement, and a formal board resolution; the bank verifies the SAFE annual FDI census and the genuineness of the remittance request. Practical hurdles include five-year retention of underlying trade documents, total-amount matching of export receipts and import payments with customs declarations, and the prohibition on using settled capital for entrusted loans, equity investments, or real-estate purchases outside the approved business scope. With a disciplined documentary pipeline, the WFOE can operate a compliant treasury within this controlled convertibility environment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China currently imposes zero mandatory surrender. The WFOE may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency or sell them voluntarily at market rates. The statutory control mechanism is SAFE's goods-trade total-amount verification system; receipts must be credited, reported, and reconciled against export customs declarations. Advance collections or delayed collections differing from the customs declaration date by more than 90 days must be reported through the bank under SAFE's trade credit and debit reporting rules. Persistent mismatches can degrade the company from A-class to B/C-class and trigger per-transaction verification, documentary scrutiny, and reduced clearing flexibility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account (Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement) and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Export Proceeds Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: RATING: LOW / VOID FOR THE MAINLAND ENTITY. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not licensed banks in China and cannot legally hold RMB deposits, settle domestic invoices, or clear cross-border trade and capital payments for the WFOE on a principal basis. PBOC, CBIRC, and SAFE regulations require all domestic receivables and payables to be settled through licensed Chinese commercial banks with qualified FX business. Offshore EMIs may be used only in the offshore holding company's treasury as payment utilities, not as the WFOE's bank. Any attempt to route trade proceeds or injected equity through a non-bank EMI into the mainland entity will create bank sanctions risk, FX-control violations, and PBOC enforcement exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory for the legal representative or the authorized director with full banking power when opening the corporate RMB basic account and the FDI capital account. PBOC anti-money-laundering rules and the corporate UBO filing regime require a face-to-face interview with the relevant natural person. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a full substitute; notarized and apostilled powers of attorney may support an authorized officer, but the bank compliance committee will still require the legal representative to appear in person or, in exceptional cross-border cases, to undergo live video verification in addition to in-branch biometric verification by the authorized officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore intermediate holding companies (for example, BVI or Cayman entities) in the WFOE ownership chain obscure ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) and source-of-funds visibility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart from every natural-person UBO to the WFOE; certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, register of directors, register of shareholders, and trust deeds for each entity in the chain; notarized and apostilled or legalized SAFE/PBOC UBO declaration; source-of-wealth dossier including bank statements, employment contracts, sale agreements, and inheritance documents; negative media, sanctions, and politically exposed persons screening results; and a signed statement confirming no nominee or fiduciary concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First-year capital disbursements are for high-value imported machinery and battery-chemical inputs, which may cause the bank to question whether the transactions match the licensed business scope and whether chemicals are subject to dual-use or export-control diversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current business license matched to ISIC 2720 and NAICS 335911 battery-cell manufacturing; import contracts and commercial invoices; customs import declarations with HS tariff codes; China import and export license; environmental impact assessment and pollution discharge permit; production plant lease, commissioning schedule, and machinery installation photographs; board-approved capital expenditure plan; and a signed end-user undertaking excluding military, weapons-of-mass-destruction, or proliferation-related uses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid conversion of newly injected FDI equity into RMB immediately after receipt may be flagged as potential capital-account round-tripping or use of funds outside the SAFE negative list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FDI registration certificate issued by SAFE or the designated bank; inbound MT103 remittance advice and bank credit confirmation; board resolution authorizing the capital-use plan; detailed cash-flow forecast and business plan; pro-forma vendor invoices and delivery milestones; certified public accountant capital verification report; and a signed negative-list compliance undertaking restricting settlement proceeds to allowable operating capex and working capital, not entrusted loans, equity investments, or real estate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty, technical-assistance, or management-fee outflows to the overseas parent may be recharacterized as hidden dividend remittance, triggering withholding-tax and transfer-pricing investigations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed technology license or service agreement; China technology import contract registration certificate; transfer-pricing local file with arm's-length benchmarking; board minutes approving the fee; Chinese VAT output on services and 10% withholding income tax payment certificates; foreign tax-residence certificates from the parent jurisdiction; and subsidiary financial statements demonstrating the services actually received and the arm's-length fee calculation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The equity injection must be remitted from the direct overseas shareholder to the WFOE's dedicated FDI capital settlement account at a licensed Tier-1 commercial bank branch. The wire should identify the WFOE full legal name, address, account number, and reference the SAFE FDI registration certificate and the SAFE balance-of-payments transaction code for inward direct investment capital contribution. Third-party remitters are prohibited. After credit, the bank logs the FDI inflow, obtains the current-account or capital-account verification, and the WFOE instructs a licensed Chinese CPA to issue a capital verification report. The WFOE may then apply for voluntary settlement of foreign-currency capital into RMB subject to the SAFE negative list. All documents, including the FDI registration certificate, board resolution, capital-use plan, bank advices, and CPA report, must be archived for inspection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import of raw materials, components, and machinery, settlement rails include bank-issued commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT701) with documents-against-acceptance or documents-against-payment terms, direct outward MT103 remittances against validated customs declarations and invoices, and documentary collections (D/P and D/A) processed through the bank's trade-services department. For export sales of sodium-ion battery cells, the preferred rail is SWIFT MT103 receipt on the company's collection account, supported by export customs declarations and sales contracts. Standby letters of credit and documentary collections may be used for open-account and cross-border trade risk mitigation. Cross-border RMB trade can alternatively be cleared through CIPS while SWIFT remains the messaging layer for non-RMB transactions. Every payment must be matched in SAFE's goods-trade monitoring system and backed by the underlying customs declarations and tax documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore CNY forward contracts with licensed Chinese banks covering 100% of genuine projected current-account and trade exposure; speculative positions are prohibited.
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps to manage timing mismatches in foreign-currency debt, interest, and equity flows, executed only on a real-demand and hedged-exposure basis.
Plain-vanilla FX options and option combinations such as risk reversals and collars, permitted under SAFE derivative rules for non-bank corporates with genuine risk.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) and offshore CNH products are not permissible for the mainland WFOE; all hedging must remain onshore, deliverable, and supported by verified underlying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report (annual return for market entities registered with SAMR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Open filing window from 1 January to 30 June immediately following the reporting fiscal year; no statutory extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by 30 June results in inclusion on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operating Activities; if not rectified within three consecutive years, the WFOE is transferred to the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List, triggering cross-departmental blacklisting, restrictions on legal representatives and directors, administrative revocation of the business license and eventual deregistration strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Settlement and Reconciliation Filing (annual corporate income tax return, financial statement schedules, and foreign investor withholding annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the competent local tax office of the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory filing and tax settlement by 31 May of the calendar year following each taxable year; financial statements and tax basis schedules must accompany the return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing correction order plus fine up to RMB 2,000, or up to RMB 10,000 for aggravated non-compliance; daily late-payment interest of 0.05% on the underpaid amount; continued default permits compulsory enforcement against bank accounts, receivables, and movable assets, and denial of exit clearance for responsible officers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report under the PRC Foreign Investment Law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) with centralized transmission to the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System during the same 1 January to 30 June annual window; any change to beneficial ownership or shareholder structure must be reported to SAMR within 30 calendar days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing exposes the WFOE to an administrative correction order and fine up to RMB 200,000, plus credit-file punishment preventing foreign exchange purchase, dividend remittance and approval of subsequent foreign-invested enterprise filings; persistent default leads to administrative cancellation of registration records

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit applies to the WFOE when any of the following quantitative thresholds is crossed as reflected in the ASBE-compliant financial statements: (i) balance-sheet total assets equal or exceed RMB 50 million; (ii) annual operating revenue (turnover) equals or exceeds RMB 100 million; or (iii) annual average headcount equals or exceeds 300 employees. Audit is also mandatory irrespective of size if the WFOE is a listed issuer, financial institution, insurance carrier, state-funded entity, or if the tax authority, foreign exchange authority or SAMR demands audited accounts in connection with foreign debt registration, capital verification, high-tech enterprise renewal or annual report verification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS), substantially converged with IFRS; small and micro enterprises may use the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Business Enterprises for internal record keeping, but the statutory financial statements, annual tax schedules and SAMR annual report financial indicators must be prepared under ASBE, denominated in RMB and retained in the statutory books

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must identify its ultimate beneficial owner(s) at incorporation and must file any subsequent change of beneficial owner, shareholding transfer, control shift or pledging arrangement with SAMR within 30 calendar days. As part of the annual June 30 information report, the company must perform an annual confirmatory reconciliation between the UBO register data, the on-site register of members, the register of directors, the register of charges and the minute book; the annual confirmation must evidence an accurate current beneficial ownership chain.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 2,400 per annum for registered address hosting and resident corporate secretarial agent services in major mainland business centers, excluding legalization, notarial and filing-related courier costs
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 15,000 per annum for an independent CPA audit of a mid-sized WFOE battery manufacturing entity under ASBE, assuming no group consolidated audit or complex cross-border financing structures

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE) may apply a reduced 15% CIT rate for sodium-ion battery manufacturing; eligible R&D expenditure may claim a 100% additional super deduction (200% total deduction); loss carryforward is extended from 5 to 10 years for HNTE and technology-focused small-and-medium enterprises; certain encouraged industries in Western/Central China can access 15% preferential rates; foreign tax credits are available for WFOEs earning foreign-source income; mainland China does not operate a patent box regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Corporate Income Tax Annual Return, Category A) plus supporting schedules; filed electronically through the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) platform of the State Taxation Administration (STA).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional CIT prepayments are filed within 15 days after each quarter-end, with annual reconciliation due by 31 May of the following calendar year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual CIT return must be filed and settled within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., 31 May of the following year); quarterly prepayments must be settled within 15 days after the end of each quarter; if the statutory last day falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline is extended by STA notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, Unified Social Credit Code, legal name of WFOE, address, industry classification (2720 battery manufacturing), place of effective management, and identity of controlling shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the non-resident ultimate parent and foreign jurisdiction on the registration schedule; ensure the WFOE does not deny China source status for its global manufacturing income; complete the beneficial ownership and related-party disclosure schedules to avoid treaty-abuse recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from sales of sodium-ion cells, scrap sales, government grants, foreign-exchange gains, and other taxable business receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export sales to foreign related distributors must be reported at arm's-length pricing; related-party revenue should be benchmarked against at least one approved OECD method; unreported related-party revenue or pricing adjustments will trigger special tax audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, including imported raw materials, electrode active materials, electrolyte, cell assembly labor, manufacturing overhead, depreciation, and energy costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported raw materials and production components purchased from non-resident affiliates must be valued under the arm's-length standard; inflated intercompany cost will be disallowed and adjusted; maintain contemporaneous CUP or TNMM benchmarking files.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses, including management fees, royalty payments, technical service fees, and head-office recharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions for fees paid to the offshore parent or sister companies are only deductible when the services are actually rendered, benefits are received, and supporting contracts, invoices, time records, and cost allocations exist; non-resident service fees without economic substance must be added back and reported to the withholding tax schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / A100000 Line 18 (Related-Party and Special Tax Adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back and adjustment lines for transfer pricing corrections, thin capitalization interest disallowance, CFC inclusions, and other special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report any voluntary transfer pricing adjustment on intercompany battery sales, management charges, or royalty payments; attach Local File/Master File if statutory thresholds are met; failure to disclose adjusted income invites Article 48 secondary adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / A100000 Line 19-20 (Super Deduction and Tax Incentives)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction for qualified R&D expenses, HNTE preferential rate election, foreign tax credit, and other tax incentive adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the 100% R&D super deduction only with a complete R&D ledger, project approval files, and raw-material/headcount allocations; document that sodium-ion chemistry research is performed in China; misclaiming incentives creates criminal false-declaration exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / A100000 Line 28-30 (Taxable Income after Loss Carryforward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate taxable income after deduction of carryforward losses, tax-exempt income, and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward general losses for 5 years, or 10 years for HNTE status, and ensure the shareholder does not attempt to offset WFOE profits against foreign parent group losses; cross-border consolidation is prohibited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / A100000 Line 31-37 (Corporate Income Tax Payable and Credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed CIT at the applicable statutory/preferential rate, minus prepayments and foreign tax credits, resulting in final tax payable or refundable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box does not settle the 10% dividend withholding tax on future profit repatriation; schedule and report all non-resident payments separately on the withholding return; treaty-reduced WHT requires a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership packet before payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return exposes the WFOE to a fine of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000-10,000 in serious cases, under PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL) Article 62; unpaid or late-paid tax accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% under Article 32; underpayment or tax evasion by false reporting carries a penalty of 50%-300% of the evaded tax under Article 63; if tax evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the tax payable, the directors and responsible parties may face criminal liability for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years in serious cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% gross-basis withholding tax on dividends distributed to a non-resident enterprise shareholder under EIT Law Articles 3 and 27, unless reduced under an applicable bilateral income tax treaty (commonly 5% for a beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the WFOE equity).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke bilateral DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) in the treaty jurisdiction; (2) complete the non-resident treaty benefit application form under STA Announcement [2015] No. 60; (3) provide a beneficial-ownership self-declaration demonstrating the recipient is not a mere conduit, with board minutes, financial statements, bank records, and substance evidence such as employees, premises, and decision-making functions; (4) deliver the package to the WFOE withholding agent before the dividend payment date; if the reduced rate cannot be applied ex ante, the non-resident may withhold at 10% and claim a refund from the STA within three years after payment, subject to a full administrative review of residence, beneficial ownership, and entitlement to treaty protection.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on outbound interest and royalty payments is 10% on the gross amount under EIT Law Articles 3 and 19; treaty-reduced rates typically range from 0%-10% for interest and 5%-10% for royalties depending on the jurisdiction and beneficial ownership (e.g., 5% for certain royalties and 7% for interest under the China-Hong Kong arrangement); technical service fees should not be re-characterized as royalties unless the payment is for the right to use an intellectual property; service fees may be taxed under the deemed-profit method at 10% WHT on an assessed 15%-30% taxable margin unless a permanent establishment or treaty business-profits protection applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory where prior-year related-party transactions exceed: RMB 200,000,000 for tangible property transfers; RMB 100,000,000 for intangible property transfers; RMB 100,000,000 for financial asset transfers; or RMB 40,000,000 for other related-party transactions (services, loans, royalties, and commissions). Master File preparation is mandatory where aggregate related-party transactions exceed RMB 1,000,000,000; contemporaneous documentation must be filed with the STA within 15 days of the annual return deadline, and any related-party transaction can be challenged regardless of thresholds where pricing is not at arm's length.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the substance-over-form doctrine operates through EIT Law Article 47 (General Anti-Avoidance Rules), Article 45 (Controlled Foreign Corporation rules), SAT Announcement [2015] No. 60 (beneficial ownership anti-abuse), and judicial anti-abuse principles. For a sodium-ion battery WFOE, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) include procurement of raw materials, production scheduling, cell chemistry R&D, quality control, inventory and logistics management, product pricing, warranty risk management, and strategic management exercised by directors and executives physically present in China. A WFOE without employees, assets, factory, operational expenditure, and decision-making functions will be treated as a shell, and its profits and treaty benefits will be recharacterized or denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: WFOE sells sodium-ion battery cells to its offshore parent or related distributor at a price below production cost while paying excessive management fees, royalties, or interest to the non-resident group; arm's-length benchmarking reports are absent or falsified, and no Local File/Master File is prepared despite statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Articles 41 and 48 authorize the STA to recharacterize the related-party transaction, adjust taxable income, impose secondary transfer pricing adjustments, and charge 5% annual interest on the tax adjustment; TCAL Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50%-300% of the evaded tax where the conduct is intentional or fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns, issue false intercompany invoices, or knowingly direct the underpricing scheme may be jointly and severally liable for the tax adjustment out of personal assets; exit bans and travel blacklisting may be imposed on directors with unsatisfied tax obligations; criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201 for tax evasion can result in imprisonment of up to 7 years, plus fines and confiscation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse and Beneficial Ownership Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: WFOE is structured as a letterbox company with no factory, employees, production assets, or operational substance; it is interposed in the ownership chain solely to access a reduced bilateral treaty withholding rate on dividends, interest, or royalties that are economically derived from Chinese manufacturing profits and ultimately destined to a non-treaty beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty benefits are denied under STA Announcement [2015] No. 60 and EIT Law Article 47; the full 10% statutory WHT becomes immediately payable, plus daily 0.05% late-payment interest and a 50%-300% penalty under TCAL Article 63 for false beneficial-ownership declarations; the non-resident entity is blacklisted in tax-integrity records and may lose all treaty access for subsequent years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false beneficial-ownership forms, sign sham dividend resolutions, or authorize dividend payments to a conduit without substance face personal civil liability for the under-withheld tax; travel bans are automatically issued for directors responsible for unpaid withholding liabilities; criminal liability for fraudulent tax avoidance and concealment under Criminal Law Article 201 can lead to imprisonment for 3-7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Deduction, Invoice Fraud, and Illegal Cross-Border Remittance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: WFOE inflates costs by fabricating contracts, using forged invoices, or characterizing dividend distributions and profit repatriation as deductible consulting, management, or technical-service fees paid to related non-resident entities; the corresponding outward foreign-exchange remittances are misreported to banks and SAFE, and the annual CIT return omits the required related-party payment disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TCAL Article 32 imposes daily late-interest charges; Article 63 imposes a 50%-300% penalty on evaded tax; Criminal Law Article 205 imposes severe criminal penalties, including imprisonment up to 10 years and fines for false invoicing; SAFE may impose penalties of 30%-100% of the illegal outward remittance under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, and the AML risk classification will be escalated to enhanced due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in the false invoice or remittance scheme are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts when the WFOE cannot satisfy the assessment; the responsible persons are placed on the tax non-payment blacklist with exit bans and travel restrictions; criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Articles 201 and 205 can result in imprisonment for up to 10 years, personal fines, and disqualification from serving as directors under PRC Company Law.
